result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier gets 30 unless you give a value, and an existing supplier can be renegotiated through `updateSupplier`. The full suite passes offline (608 tests, build success), including a new test for your Swedish example (45 days, then renegotiated to 14). Nothing is committed.

**What changed**
- `schema.sql`: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)`.
- `model/Supplier.java`: new record component `paymentTermsDays`, plus a `DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30` constant. I kept the old 5-argument constructor as a delegating overload that uses 30, so the many existing call sites in tests and `DemoScenario` still compile.
- `DataStore.java`: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the column; `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read it.
- `SupplierTest.java`: one new test covering default, renegotiation, and all four listings.

**Gap to decide on:** other queries also build `Supplier` objects, such as purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, spending and performance reports, and category suppliers. They don't select the new column, so they report the default 30 days even when a different value is stored. Your spec only covers the four listings, so I left those alone. If those reports should show the real terms too, it's the same one-column change at each of those sites.
